ChainLink.description:
One link of a stack-up chain across a product: a part's dimension or a connection.

A part link names its ``item`` and the ``dimension`` tag; the dimension's declared
tolerance is used, or, where the item declares none, the ISO 2768-1 general tolerance on
the ``nominal`` the link states. A connection link names the mate or connection and
the ± ``allowance`` it contributes, with its ``source``. ``direction`` is +1 when the
link growing widens the gap.
ChainLink.title: ChainLink

CircularPattern.description: ``count`` instances spread ``angle_deg`` apart about one of the parent's axes.
CircularPattern.title: CircularPattern

Cited.description: A declared value and the source it was read from.
Cited.title: Cited

ComponentRecord.description:
A purchased component: identity, where to buy it, the space it takes, its ratings.

``envelope`` is the box it occupies, centred on its own origin, and ``holes`` the
interfaces it offers a mate, as a placeholder's; ``envelope_source`` and ``mass_source``
name where they were read. ``ratings`` must include every rating
:data:`FAMILY_RATINGS` lists for ``family``, each with its source.
ComponentRecord.title: ComponentRecord

Connection.description:
Two interfaces that meet, each as ``item.interface``: ``place`` is placed on ``on``.

The item is an instance of the product that declares the connection. The mate is
derived from the pair: a pattern meets a pattern hole by hole, a face meets a face, a
shaft runs in its bore. The pairing's checks go on that product's card. ``joint``
declares how the placed item moves; any joint but a rigid one needs two interfaces that
define an axis.
Connection.title: Connection

Definition.description:
One item defined once: a catalog part's spec, a sub-product, a placeholder, or a
purchased component.

``component`` is a :class:`~anvilate.components.ComponentRecord`: placed as its envelope
with its holes, and checked by its ratings against ``demands``, what the product asks
of it. Only a component states demands, and a component is bought.
Definition.title: Definition

Demand.description: What the product asks of a component, and where that requirement came from.
Demand.title: Demand

Expansion.description: A material's coefficient of thermal expansion, as the declaration read it, cited.
Expansion.title: Expansion

Instance.description:
A definition placed in its parent, once or as a pattern, under a name.

``mirrored`` is refused: an opposite-hand part is a different part to make and to buy,
so it is its own definition with its own number, never a negatively scaled instance.
Instance.title: Instance

Interface.description:
One interface an item offers: its name, kind, where it is, and its parameters.

A ``face`` kind names the face it is on (``top``, ``bottom``…); a pattern kind also
lists the item's ``holes`` it is made of, by tag. An ``axis`` kind names the item's own
axis it runs along. ``parameters`` are the kind's required values (:data:`KINDS`).
Interface.title: Interface

ItemIdentity.description:
The identity a PDM, PLM or ERP carries: part number, revision, description, source.

``part_number`` may be left out; the tree then gives the definition a provisional
number derived from its content, marked provisional wherever it is shown.
ItemIdentity.title: ItemIdentity

ItemSource.description: Whether a definition is made, bought, or carried for reference only.
ItemSource.title: ItemSource

Joint.description:
How a connection moves: rigid, or about or along the axis its interfaces share.

A ``revolute`` joint turns and a ``linear`` one slides along the axis; a ``cylindrical``
one does both and a ``ball`` turns about its point. ``range`` is a revolute or
cylindrical joint's turn, as angles, or a linear joint's travel, as lengths, from the
placed position; the placed product sweeps the moving item through it.
Joint.title: Joint

Layout.description: The product's driving parameters and datums, read by name and never itself a part.
Layout.title: Layout

LayoutDatum.description:
A named datum items mate to: a point, an axis or a plane, fixed in the product's frame.

``at`` is where it is. An ``axis`` runs along ``direction`` through it, and a ``plane``
is normal to ``direction`` through it. A mate names the datum as its ``on`` part: a
plane offers the two faces normal to it (``top`` and ``bottom`` for a ``z`` plane), an
axis offers itself to a ``shaft_in_bore`` mate, and a point offers any face or axis
through it. Its coordinates may read layout parameters like any other value.
LayoutDatum.title: LayoutDatum

LayoutParameter.description:
A driving parameter: a name, a value, where it comes from, and what reads it.

An item reads it by writing ``{layout: <name>}`` where a value goes in its spec or its
placeholder; :func:`parse_product` puts the value there and records the place in
``read_by`` as ``<definition>:<dotted path>``. The product checks every recorded place
still holds the value, so a stored product cannot claim a reader it does not have.
LayoutParameter.title: LayoutParameter

Limit.description: A declared limit on the product as a whole, and where it comes from.
Limit.title: Limit

LinearPattern.description: ``count`` instances ``spacing`` apart along one of the parent's axes.
LinearPattern.title: LinearPattern

MassGrowth.description: The growth allowance a mass carries by its maturity, as fractions, and their source.
MassGrowth.title: MassGrowth

Mate.description:
How one part meets a part already placed.

``place`` is the part being placed and ``on`` a part that already is. ``face_to_face``
puts two faces in contact. ``edge_flush`` lines two faces up in one plane. ``hole_pattern``
puts ``place.face`` on ``on.face`` with the listed holes coaxial, pair by pair.
``shaft_in_bore`` makes two axes one. ``offset`` opens a gap between mated faces, and
``rotation_deg`` turns the part about a shared axis that nothing else fixes.

``fit`` is the ISO 286 fit a ``shaft_in_bore`` mate is made to, hole zone then shaft
zone, such as ``H7/g6``. The bore and the shaft are drawn at one nominal size; the fit
says how much room, or how much interference, their tolerances leave between them.
Mate.title: Mate

MateEnd.description:
One side of a mate: a part, and the feature on it that meets the other part.

``face`` is one of the part's six outermost faces by direction: ``top``, ``bottom``,
``left``, ``right``, ``front`` or ``back``. ``holes`` are hole tags, as the part's
features carry them, in the order they pair with the other side's. ``axis`` is one of
the part's own axes (``x``, ``y`` or ``z``) through its origin, which is the axis of a
round part; ``feature`` names a hole or bore instead, by its tag.
MateEnd.title: MateEnd

MaterialDeclaration.description:
What a material is made of and what it withstands, each value with its source.

``material`` is the id the product's items name. ``plastic`` counts it in the recycled
plastic roll-up. ``attributes`` are the material's own declared values, read by the
material needs: ``service_max_temperature``, ``total_mass_loss`` (a fraction),
``flammability`` (a UL 94 class) and ``biocompatibility`` (a body-contact category).
MaterialDeclaration.title: MaterialDeclaration

MaterialNeeds.description:
What the product's materials must withstand, each need with its limit and source.

``items`` limits the needs to those items (all of them when empty). Each need is a
:class:`Cited` limit: ``service_temperature`` and ``sterilization`` a temperature the
material's service maximum must reach; ``vacuum`` the largest total mass loss allowed;
``flammability`` the least UL 94 class; ``body_contact`` the category the material must
be declared for.
MaterialNeeds.title: MaterialNeeds

OpenInterface.description: An interface left unconnected on purpose, as ``item.interface``, and why.
OpenInterface.title: OpenInterface

PartInterface.description:
An interface on a catalog part, bound to the part's tagged features.

Its frame and parameters are read from the built features, never restated: a pattern's
holes and the face they open on, an axial kind's axis and diameter. A ``mounting_face``
names its ``face`` and no feature. ``face`` may also name the far face of a pattern of
through holes, along the same axis.
PartInterface.title: PartInterface

Placeholder.description:
An item not yet detailed: an envelope, a mass, and why it is still a placeholder.

``holes`` are the interfaces it offers, so a bought motor's bolt pattern can take a
hole-pattern mate before the motor is chosen. ``center_of_mass`` is measured from the
envelope's centre; left out, the centre is used and the placed product says so.
Placeholder.title: Placeholder

PlaceholderHole.description:
A hole a placeholder offers to a mate: its tag, where it is, its size, the face it is in.

``x``, ``y`` and ``z`` are the hole's entry point in the placeholder's frame, whose origin
is the envelope's centre; ``face`` is the envelope face it opens on, which sets its axis.
PlaceholderHole.title: PlaceholderHole

Price.description:
A unit price for screening cost: the amount, its currency, its source and its date.

It is the user's figure, a quote or a catalog price as of ``date``; a cost roll-up
sums prices in one currency and converts none.
Price.title: Price

ProductChain.description:
A one-dimensional stack-up through a product's items and connections, and the band
its gap must land in, with ``source`` saying where the band comes from; ``samples`` and
``seed`` add a seeded Monte Carlo run.
ProductChain.title: ProductChain

ProductLoad.description: A load the product carries: on an item, as a force down or a mass under gravity.
ProductLoad.title: ProductLoad

Quantity.description:
A physical value: a magnitude and the unit it was expressed in.

Construct directly (``Quantity(magnitude=75, unit="kip")``) or parse from
text (``Quantity.parse("75 kip")``). The stored ``unit`` string is exactly
what the user wrote, canonicalized only to Pint's spelling of it.
Quantity.title: Quantity

Rating.description: One rating the component is sold with, and the datasheet line it was read from.
Rating.title: Rating

Reference.description:
An existing assembly the product is designed against, read from a STEP file.

``file`` is the STEP assembly's path relative to the product's folder. It is placed and
mated by its envelope's faces like any item, every solid in it is checked for
interference, and its ``clearance`` is the least gap the product's own items must keep
to it. It is never made: it is out of the release's STEP and is a reference line on the
BOM.
Reference.title: Reference

Screening.description:
What the product as a whole is held to.

``mass_growth`` is the growth allowance per mass maturity; ``max_mass`` is checked on
the predicted mass, basic plus growth, as a budget whose terms are the bodies;
``max_cg_height`` is the highest the centre of mass may sit above the product's lowest
point; ``min_tilt`` is the tilt the centre of mass must
stay inside the footprint up to; ``min_clearance`` the least gap between any two items
that share no connection. ``loads`` are what the product carries, which travel down
through the bodies they rest on to the floor; ``splits`` divide a body's load among
more supports than determine it, each with its basis. ``vertical_acceleration`` is the
acceleration the load path is carried at, gravity included and acting down: each body's
weight and each load given as a mass are carried at m·a rather than m·g.
Screening.title: Screening

Split.description: How a body's load divides among more supports than determine it, and on what basis.
Split.title: Split

Sterilization.description: A sterilization the material must survive: the method, its temperature, the source.
Sterilization.title: Sterilization

Substance.description: One substance in a material: its CAS number, its name, its mass fraction.
Substance.title: Substance

SupplierNumber.description: Where to buy it: a supplier and that supplier's part number.
SupplierNumber.title: SupplierNumber

Thermal.description:
The temperature range the product sees, the slip its connections allow, and the
expansion coefficients of its materials, each cited.
Thermal.title: Thermal

Variant.description:
A named variant: layout parameters overridden and definitions substituted.

``parameters`` gives new values to layout parameters by name. ``substitutions`` are
definitions that replace the base definitions with the same ``id``. A variant is resolved
to a complete product of its own by :func:`resolve_variant`.
Variant.title: Variant

VendorModel.description:
The vendor's STEP file for the component: a path in the user's folder, and its hash.

The file is used where it is, never copied. ``sha256`` is the file's digest when the
record was written, so a file changed since reads as changed rather than as the model.
VendorModel.title: VendorModel

Generated from anvilate.product.Product.
